name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that dual service in legislative and executive departments violates separation of powers, but the specific employments in this case with NSHE and local government do not constitute such a violation.

name: HERNDON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the district court violated the principle of party presentation and that the majority's analysis of the separation-of-powers issue was procedurally and substantively flawed, requiring reversal and remand for further factual development.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Dissented, argued that NSHE should be considered part of the executive branch and that the majority's analysis for Neal, Torres, and Miller was incorrect, requiring further factual development. Concurred that Ohrenschall's dual service was compatible.

name: LEE, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority oversimplified the separation-of-powers issue by focusing on the department rather than the individual's specific functions, siding with Justice Herndon for reversal and remand. Concurred on party presentation and ancillary issues.

name: Pickering
description: Concurred, argued that the Nevada Constitution's eminent domain amendment does not prohibit a regulated public utility from taking private property for a statutorily defined public use, and a jury trial is not required when there are no genuine issues of material fact regarding public use.

name: Stiglich
description: Concurred, arguing that the challenged statutes are not unconstitutionally vague and provide fair notice of what is prohibited, as their terms are readily ascertainable through ordinary and industry meanings, and they include a scienter requirement.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the initiative petition has a single subject, a legally sufficient description of effect, and does not require an expenditure of money.

name: CADISH, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the prosecutorial-consent requirement for informal supervision is not a sentencing decision and therefore does not violate the separation of powers doctrine.

name: STIGLICH, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that both the governor and the chief justice have concurrent constitutional authority to designate temporary substitutes for disqualified supreme court justices.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that while both the governor and chief justice have appointment powers, the selection method should be random and uniform, and a replacement was not necessary in this case as a quorum existed.

name: CAD1SH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that a private right of action for money damages exists to vindicate search-and-seizure violations under the Nevada Constitution, and qualified immunity does not apply to such an action.

name: Parraguirre, C.J.
description: Concurred, delivering the majority opinion that mandated changes to hand-count livestreaming and signature verification, while denying relief on the touchscreen issue.

name: HARDESTY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the district court properly enjoined the initiative because it was an unfunded mandate, had a misleading description of effect, and impaired the Legislature's deliberative function.

name: HERNDON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the initiative was valid because the funding mandate does not apply to constitutional amendments, the description of effect was adequate, and initiatives can direct the Legislature to enact laws.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the initiative was valid because the funding mandate does not apply to constitutional amendments, the description of effect was adequate, and initiatives can direct the Legislature to enact laws.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that NRS 295.026 is a constitutional exercise of legislative power to facilitate the initiative process, and withdrawn petitions are void, nullifying the Secretary of State's duty to place them on the ballot.

name: HARDESTY, J.
description: Dissented, argued that NRS 295.026 is unconstitutional because it obstructs the Secretary of State's mandatory constitutional duty to place verified initiative petitions on the ballot if the Legislature does not act.

name: SILVER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that NRS 295.026 is unconstitutional because it obstructs the Secretary of State's mandatory constitutional duty to place verified initiative petitions on the ballot if the Legislature does not act.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Dissented, argued that NRS 295.026 is unconstitutional because it obstructs the Secretary of State's mandatory constitutional duty to place verified initiative petitions on the ballot if the Legislature does not act.

name: HARDESTY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Nevada Constitution textually commits broad, discretionary authority over public education, including funding, to the Legislature, making the claims nonjusticiable political questions.

name: CADISH, J.
description: Dissented, argued that education is a fundamental right imposing a judicially enforceable, mandatory duty on the Legislature to provide a basic education, and therefore the issue is not a nonjusticiable political question.

name: SILVER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Nevada Constitution's separation of powers clause prohibits a legislator from simultaneously serving as a prosecutor, and the court should have addressed the merits of the challenge and determined an appropriate remedy.

name: HERNDON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's focus solely on the petitioner's requested remedy was shortsighted and ignored the constitutional issue, which warrants extraordinary relief to protect the integrity of the judicial process.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Dissented, agreed with the opinions of Justice Silver and Justice Herndon.

name: CADISH, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that public policy does not warrant creating a civil forfeiture exception to the homestead exemption, and incarcerated individuals can be deemed residents for homestead purposes.

name: HARDESTY, J.
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion that expanded the public-importance exception to standing for separation-of-powers challenges that are likely to recur and require future guidance, even if they do not involve legislative expenditures.

name: HARDESTY, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the district court erred by misinterpreting Marsy's Law to include anyone impacted by a crime, failing to determine if impact statement authors were statutory or constitutional victims, and not assessing the relevance and reliability of non-victim statements, thus requiring resentencing.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that employee status for MWA claims is determined by the economic realities test, and for NRS Chapter 608 claims, by either the economic realities test or NRS 608.0155, neither of which are conclusively affected by contractual recitations or NTA lease approvals.

name: Cadish, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the MWA's 'all remedies available' provision constitutionally incorporates waiting time penalties, and NRS 608.0155 cannot extinguish this constitutional remedy.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the majority opinion does not foreclose the availability of waiting time penalties as a remedy under the MWA's 'all remedies' clause, given how the claims were pleaded.

name: SILVER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that general tailoring arguments are impermissible under Nevada's Constitution.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that general tailoring arguments are impermissible under Nevada's Constitution.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the economic realities test applies to the MWA, finding the dancers are employees, and NRS 608.0155 cannot abrogate constitutional minimum wage protections.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while the Legislature intended NRS 608.0155 to limit the MWA's scope, it lacked the constitutional power to do so, reaching the same result as the majority through a different path.
